hard-gates-precede-soft-scores.statement: Eligibility — applicant type, geography, award-size capacity, deadline — is decided by deterministic checks that no scoring model may override. Fit is argued only after eligibility passes; a beautifully matched application the applicant may not submit is worth nothing.

honest-null-over-forced-guess.statement: Classification, extraction and matching prefer "unknown" with low confidence over a weak guess. A wrong category routes money away from the right applicant; an honest null routes a human to look. Unknown codes never fall through to a default class.

small-samples-stay-silent.statement: A rate computed over too few outcomes is suppressed, not published: win rates below a minimum of decided outcomes, aggregates below a k-anonymity floor, confidence bands tied to sample size. Publishing a 100% win rate over two applications is a lie told with true numbers.

never-fabricate-a-figure.statement: No statistic, past result, date, identifier or named partner is ever invented. Where a specific figure would strengthen the case and none is provided, a bracketed placeholder for the writer beats a made-up number — a wrong figure the applicant accepts as theirs is worse than a blank they fill in. Verified organizational facts are the authoritative figure set; nothing else is stated as fact.

untrusted-text-is-data.statement: Funder RFPs, scraped listings and applicant-supplied documents enter prompts as delimited, untrusted data. Nothing inside them may change the task, the score, or the output format; forged delimiters are stripped at the boundary.

clean-is-not-ready.statement: A compliance report with zero findings certifies nothing unless every applicable check actually executed. Check coverage is part of the verdict; "no issues found" and "not checked" must be impossible to confuse.

provenance-per-field.statement: Every pre-filled or extracted value carries its confidence and its source. Onboarding and drafting become review of sourced values, not data entry — and a value whose source cannot be shown is a candidate, not a fact.

the-funder-sets-the-form.statement: An application's structure, register and emphasis come from the funder family's own scoring rubric — a federal reviewer, a foundation program officer, an arts panel and a movement funder read differently, and one generic template misfits all of them. Genre is detected conservatively; the safe default is the modest register.
